items.title: Phil Schaap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: his fame in the Ramsey Lewis area kind of allowed people to know

ctx.x: I’d like to think that but it probably wasn’t.

It wasn’t. In the late sixties I’m catching a couple of more sets. Now maybe it was ad libbed in the early sixties and then it was pat. But I thought he was far more thoughtful about the music than his fame in the Ramsey Lewis area kind of allowed people to know. He’s sort of seen as one of the springboards of the pop-fusion developments that are going to occur. Nowhere near as important as Miles but he’s there and he lasts until ’75, and his band did go a little bit electric and of course and had its “Mercy…
